message.content: The t8 probe shows massive tolerance violations even on ordinary random inputs, which would mean a real bug. Before concluding, I'll run one independent sanity probe (own reference, not kernel.reference) on simple inputs with known closed-form DFTs, to rule out a probe/reference mismatch.

function.arguments:
{"claim_id": "c1", "code": "import torch, sys, json
sys.path.insert(0, "/root/cases/case_163")
import kernel
dev="cuda"
def check(name, v):
    v = v.to(dev)
    out = kernel.run(v)
    ref = torch.fft.rfft(v.double(), dim=1, norm="backward")
    ref = torch.stack([ref.real, ref.imag], dim=-1)
    err = (out.double()-ref).abs()
    tol = 1e-4 + 1e-6*ref.abs()
    bad = (err>tol)|~torch.isfinite(out)
    r = {"case":name,"max_err":err.max().item(),"rel_worst":(err/tol).max().item(),"violations":int(bad.sum())}
    print(json.dumps(r)); return int(bad.sum())
tot=0
# constant row: DC=N*v, all other bins zero
v = torch.full((2,64),3.0,dtype=torch.float16)
tot+=check("const_n64",v)
v = torch.full((2,256),3.0,dtype=torch.float16)
tot+=check("const_n256",v)
# alternating row (+1,-1): only Nyquist bin nonzero = N
v = torch.tensor([[1.0,-1.0]*128],dtype=torch.float16)
tot+=check("alternating_n256",v)
# single impulse
v = torch.zeros((1,128),dtype=torch.float16); v[0,5]=1.0
tot+=check("impulse_n128",v)
# random
g=torch.Generator().manual_seed(7)
for n in (64,128,256):
    v=torch.randn((4,n),generator=g).to(torch.float16)
    tot+=check(f"rand_n{n}",v)
print(json.dumps({"TOTAL_VIOLATIONS":tot}))", "timeout_s": 120}
